NEW DELHI: Congress leader Amrinder Singh Raja Warring on Thursday changed his X bio to "former Punjab Pradesh Congress Committee President" amid speculation that the Congress high command has asked the Ludhiana MP to step down from the top party post in the state amid a factional feud.This comes hours after Warring declined to comment on reports that the party high command had decided to replace him, saying that “some issues are internal”.The move comes after months of infighting within the Punjab Congress, which intensified after the party high command decided on July 1 to retain Warring as the state unit chief.A section of leaders led by former chief minister Charanjit Singh Channi had opposed Warring’s continuation and sought his removal. Leaders aligned with the Channi camp also stayed away from party programmes led by Warring.According to PTI, the Congress general secretary and Punjab in-charge held a series of meetings with state leaders before submitting his report to the party high command on the proposed leadership change.The high command subsequently informed Warring of its decision, party sources told PTI, adding that the Congress is now looking to appoint a leader who can bring different factions together ahead of the 2027 assembly polls.Former minister and ex-MP Vijay Inder Singla has emerged as a frontrunner for the post, sources said. The other names being discussed include former Olympian and Jalandhar Cantt MLA Pargat Singh, former MLA Rana KP Singh, Raja Sansi MLA Sukhbinder Singh Sarkaria, former chief minister Charanjit Singh Channi and Gurdaspur MP Sukhjinder Singh Randhawa.The leadership tussle has played out publicly in recent months, raising concerns within the party over its impact on the Congress campaign as it seeks to return to power in Punjab.The factionalism has also added to concerns over the party’s ability to consolidate its organisation ahead of the assembly polls.Asked about the possibility of a change in the Punjab Congress leadership on Tuesday, Channi said the decision was the prerogative of the party high command.“It is the prerogative of Rahul Gandhi and (Mallikarjun) Kharge ji. Only they know who is to be appointed or when is to be changed,” Channi told reporters in Delhi.Warring had also faced criticism from sections of the party over the Congress’ electoral performance in Punjab and his leadership.In August, he defended himself against criticism over the party’s decline in the 2022 assembly elections, questioning attempts to hold him responsible for the loss.“The only mistake is that when the Congress Party had 80 seats, we came down from 80 to 18 seats. Is that my fault? Captain Amarinder Singh led the government twice. From 80 seats, we came down to 18 seats,” he had said.
Article Summary: Congress leader Amrinder Singh Raja Warring changed his X bio to "former Punjab Pradesh Congress Committee President" This comes amid speculation that the Congress high command has asked the Ludhiana MP to step down from the top party post in the state. Former minister and ex-MP Vijay Inder Singla has emerged as a frontrunner for the post, sources said.

NEW DELHI: India produced another strong medal haul at the Asian Games 2026 on Monday, winning eight medals across athletics, shooting and kurash. However, the impressive collection did not bring any change in the overall standings, with India remaining 12th as the country continued to wait for another gold medal.India added four silver and four bronze medals during the day but could not increase its gold tally. After Day 9, India stood at 45 medals — four gold, 20 silver and 21 bronze.'The eight-medal haul included silver medals for Yashvir Singh, Murali Sreeshankar, Gulveer Singh and Esha Singh, while Rohit Yadav, Parul Chaudhary, Vithya Ramraj and Pincky Balhara won bronze.India's strongest showing came in the men's javelin, where Yashvir and Rohit produced a double podium finish in the absence of defending champion Neeraj Chopra.Yashvir recorded a personal best of 85.72m for silver, while Rohit won bronze with 84.35m. Sri Lanka's Rumesh Pathirage claimed gold with 88.55m.Sreeshankar also won silver in the men's long jump with 8.07m despite an injury forcing him to abandon his final two attempts. China's Yuhao Shi took gold with 8.17m.Gulveer added his second silver of the Games with a personal best of 3:36.72 in the men's 1500m, having earlier finished runner-up in the 10,000m.Parul Chaudhary won bronze in the women's 5000m with 15:14.61, adding to the bronze she had claimed in the 3000m steeplechase.Vithya Ramraj also took bronze in the women's 400m hurdles with a personal best of 54.75 seconds.Esha Singh secured silver in the women's 25m pistol after finishing with 38 hits, the same score as China's Xiao Jiaruixuan, who won the gold after the shoot-off.Pincky Balhara added bronze in the women's -78kg kurash category, losing 0-5 to South Korea's Sumin Mo in the semifinals.Despite the eight medals, India's gold tally remained at four, a crucial factor in the standings as countries are ranked by gold medals first.China led with 132 golds, followed by Japan with 41, South Korea with 21 and Uzbekistan with 12. India remained 12th with 45 medals, highlighting how a large haul of silver and bronze medals has yet to translate into a significant rise in the standings.
Article Summary: India added four silver and four bronze medals during the day but could not increase its gold tally. After Day 9, India stood at 45 medals — four gold, 20 silver and 21 bronze. The eight-medal haul included silver medals for Yashvir Singh, Murali Sreeshankar, Gulveer Singh and Esha Singh.

Article Title: ‘This is not cricket’: Gautam Gambhir questions Guwahati pitch after India chase 406 with ease
Article Text:
India's coach Gautam Gambhir, left, chats with captain Shubman Gill during a practice session. (AP Photo)

‘It’s not fair for the bowlers’

Gambhir backs exposure for young bowlers

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: India head coach Gautam Gambhir had little doubt about the entertainment value of Wednesday’s extraordinary run-fest in Guwahati, but he was far less impressed by the conditions that allowed both teams to score more than 400 runs.After West Indies posted 405 for seven, India chased down the target in just 43.3 overs, winning by eight wickets to seal the three-match ODI series 2-0. Shubman Gill smashed an unbeaten 223 off 133 balls, while Rohit Sharma scored 101 off 75 as India completed the highest successful run chase in their ODI history.Yet, for Gambhir, the remarkable numbers also highlighted a concern. He felt the pitch offered too little to the bowlers and called for a greater balance between bat and ball.“Look, if I have to be absolutely honest, I feel I think there has to be a bit of more contest between bat and ball, because I think you talk about cricket - but this is not cricket, this is only batting,” Gambhir told Star Sports after the match.“Because imagine a young bowler bowling on this wicket, and the opposition getting 400 and then we go on to chase 400. Obviously, for the records it's outstanding, for the crowd it's outstanding, for the broadcaster it's outstanding, but if you ask me as a genuine cricket fan and as a coach, because I have to have sympathy for the bowlers as well.”“When you bowl on this kind of a wicket, it's not fair for the bowlers. So we've got to give something to the bowlers so there's at least something which the bowlers can work with,” he added.The Guwahati surface produced a stunning batting display, with West Indies reaching 405 for seven before India responded with 406 for two.John Campbell, Shai Hope and Amir Jangoo struck centuries for West Indies, while Gill and Rohit then led the Indian chase. Gill's unbeaten 223 was the defining innings of the day, while his opening partnership of 255 with Rohit was India's second-highest in men's ODIs. Virat Kohli , who had scored a century in the first ODI, contributed 29 off 19 balls before falling, while Ruturaj Gaikwad made 31 off 37.The match became only the second successful chase of a target of 400 or more in men's ODI history, after South Africa's famous 438-run chase against Australia in 2006.For Gambhir, however, the scale of the scoring made it important to consider what the conditions meant for the bowlers rather than simply celebrating the batting numbers.“The first thing is that you need some sympathy and a bit of margin for the bowlers,” he said.“Often you can't be hard on bowlers, because sometimes bowling figures are such that they haven't bowled as poorly as their figures suggest. Because the margin is very small.”He also pointed to the restrictions modern-day bowlers face in ODI cricket, including fielding restrictions, two new balls and the increasing power of batters.“Plus, I think you can only bowl in good areas because besides that, with five fielders inside, two new balls, and the kind of power-hitting there is now, bowlers don't really have many options,” Gambhir said.“That is why, as a coach, as a support staff, the first thing you look at is, were they able to execute their bowling or their plans properly? If they were able to do that, then you shouldn't be hard on them.”“If you get too hard just looking at their analysis, then we will never be able to develop bowlers.”India gave Auqib Nabi his ODI debut despite already leading the series 1-0, and Gambhir said putting inexperienced bowlers into difficult situations was an important part of India's preparation for the 2027 ODI World Cup.“Imagine Auqib [Nabi] playing his first game... somewhere you need to give them a bit of support and keep a bit of an extra cushion or extra options for them,” he said. “But unfortunately, today there wasn't much for any bowler.”Gambhir said India could have waited until the third ODI, when the series would already be decided, to give Nabi an opportunity. But he argued that a dead rubber would not recreate the pressure young players could experience at a World Cup.“We could have given Auqib a chance in the next match too when it's a dead rubber, but in a dead rubber, you don't have that pressure which comes with the pressure of winning a series,” he said.“And we all know that the World Cup is all about pressure. Cricket isn't going to change like that, only the pressure will be different because the World Cup comes once in four years, so we want to put bowlers under pressure.”He also cited Gurnoor Brar as an example of a young bowler who could benefit from being exposed to demanding phases of an ODI.“For example, Gurnoor [Brar]. Having Gurnoor bowl in the first 10 overs, bowling at the death, I know people will talk about his analysis, but the more he bowls in tough conditions, in tough situations, the better it is for Indian cricket,” Gambhir said.“Because you can have him bowl in the middle overs and get good analysis or good stats for him, make him bowl defensively, but the more we expose them at such times, the better it is for Indian cricket.”
Article Summary: India coach Gautam Gambhir unhappy with conditions in Guwahati. Both West Indies and India scored more than 400 runs in Wednesday's match. India chased down the target in 43.3 overs to win by eight wickets. Shubman Gill hit an unbeaten 223 as India won the match by eight runs.

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday said he had spoken to the wife and parents of Captain Smit Machchhar, the pilot of a Dubai-Tel Aviv flydubai flight that survived an apparent hijacking attempt a day ago. PM Modi also praised the wounded pilot, saying he had "prevented another 9/11" — a reference to the September 11, 2001, terrorist attacks in New York City, when Al-Qaeda terrorists hijacked passenger planes and crashed them into the World Trade Center, killing thousands.“The incident that occurred yesterday, Captain Smit of India demonstrated remarkable patience, presence of mind, and courage; indeed, as the Prime Minister of Israel stated today, an Indian prevented a 9/11-style tragedy. For every citizen of our country, Smit's valor fills us with immense pride,” he said at the centenary celebrations of the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) in the capital.“Today, I had a conversation with his father Bhupendrabhai, his mother Gitaben, and his wife Sonalben. His medical treatment is currently ongoing, and today the entire world feels proud of him,” the prime minister added.PM Modi also appealed to citizens to pray for the pilot’s recovery.Earlier in the day, the prime minister wrote in a post on X that India is "proud of Captain Machchhar.""Captain Smit Machchhar is a HERO. In the face of the gravest danger and despite being seriously injured, he showed immense courage and an unwavering resolve to protect the lives of others. His valour helped save hundreds of lives and avert a great tragedy. India is proud of Captain Machchhar. Praying for his speedy recovery, renewed strength and good health," he wrote.Captain Machchhar, the pilot of flydubai Flight FZ1073 from Dubai to Israel's Tel Aviv, was stabbed by his co-pilot, reportedly an Omani national, in the cockpit on Wednesday. Despite his injuries, he managed to unlock the cockpit door, allowing passengers and crew members to intervene.The aircraft was subsequently diverted and made a safe emergency landing at Tabuk in Saudi Arabia. Machchhar is currently receiving medical treatment at a hospital in Tabuk.

Article Title: Monsoon deficit at 13%, officially a drought year
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The rainy season in India technically ended on Wednesday, with the summer (southwest) monsoon rainfall during June-Sept period recording a deficit of nearly 13% - a level of shortfall which is considered a drought. Significantly, this is the fourth lowest seasonal rainfall since 2001 and the 13th lowest since 1901.The situation is likely to be better during winter when northeast monsoon hits south Peninsular India between Oct 15 and Oct 21, with the IMD predicting 'normal' rainfall over Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Karaikal, coastal Andhra Pradesh and Rayalaseema region, Kerala and south interior Karnataka during Oct-Dec period. However, the winter monsoon will bring cheer to limited regions.Though most other parts of India are expected to receive 'below-normal' rainfall during the Oct-Dec period, some areas of northwest India (Punjab, parts of Haryana, Uttarakhand, Himachal and J&K) and southern parts of peninsular India are likely to get "normal to above-normal" rainfall. Incidentally, Punjab and peninsular India had to face huge rainfall deficit during the summer monsoon season, which led to drought in many districts.Overall, south Peninsular India receives 30% of its annual rainfall during northeast (winter) monsoon season. TN, Puducherry and Karaikal receive 48% of their annual rainfall during northeast monsoon season. So, normal winter monsoon this year may bring relief to the region, which received the fourth lowest summer monsoon rainfall since 1901.“We cannot forecast exact date of arrival of winter monsoon in south Peninsula at this stage. It generally coincides with final withdrawal of summer monsoon and may hit the region any day during Oct 15-21,” said IMD chief Mrutyunjay Mohapatra. Though India as a whole received nearly 13% less than normal rainfall, east and northeast India faced the highest deficit of 25%, followed by south Peninsula (24%), northwest India (6%) and central India (3%). Mohapatra said there has been a recent trend of east & northeast India consistently reporting decrease in rainfall.
Article Summary: Winter rain may bring relief to southern India. IMD predicts 'normal' rainfall over Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Karaikal, coastal Andhra Pradesh and Rayalaseema region. Punjab and peninsular India had to face huge rainfall deficit during the summer monsoon season, which led to drought.

NEW DELHI: The INDIA bloc, led by the Congress, has announced a mega action plan to take forward its campaign against “vote chori” and Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The key stakeholders of the INDIA bloc met today in the national capital to chalk out a roadmap for nationwide protests against the Election Commission’s “flawed and partisan” approach.The INDIA bloc's renewed offensive comes days after an Indian Express report citing internal differences within the Election Commission of India (ECI) regarding the implementation of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and modifications to voter registration processes. The opposition parties' meeting also comes in the backdrop of successful mobilisation programmed led by the Cockroach Janata Party against NEET paper leak, which brought the GenZ to the streets and forced the government to accept their demands.After hours long deliberations, Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge unveiled the opposition’s blueprint for intensified demonstrations against EC’s ‘malpractices’ and shared details of how the INDIA bloc will stand up against electoral irregularities.Here is what the INDIA bloc allies decided on their action plan against EC’s ‘partisan approach and malpractices’Then there was also a list of 6 demands which the opposition parties announced. It includedSo far, so good. But the problem is that all these demands have already been raised by various opposition parties from time to time without any success.We have heard several leaders in the past demanding a return to ballot paper. This has not happened and is unlikely to happen.The fight over alleged discrepancies in the SIR process has been an ongoing one. We have seen Rahul Gandhi and other regional leaders raise the issue. But none of them have managed to sustain the momentum or stop the process. Even the courts have refused to back their allegations and have not stopped the SIR process.Now, let’s focus on the action plan.Protests at district level, march to Election Commission’s office, rallies, appeal in Supreme Court - all make for good optics, but can they bring about enough pressure?The Congress, which is leading the opposition block, has been consistent in raising these issues, but has failed to keep the momentum going. Rahul Gandhi has addressed several press conferences in the last two years leading the charge against the Election Commission and Gyanesh Kumar. His yatra in Bihar ahead of assembly elections last year brought the issue to centre stage but once again the momentum did not sustain.Clearly, the Congress and the other opposition parties need to think how to run a sustained campaign for mobilisation.At the CWC meeting held on Tuesday, ahead of today’s INDIA bloc meeting, Rahul Gandhi had claimed that revelations about the Election Commission were now coming out in the open because of the Congress. During the two-and-a-half hour CWC meeting, Rahul pointed out that the Congress had been raising the "vote chori" issue strongly with facts and talked about irregularities in polls in Haryana, Karnataka and Maharashtra but many were sceptical of it.Leader of opposition in Lok Sabha claimed that EVM and voters' list "match-fixing" of polls was underway in the country and asserted that his party should not budge from the path of "virodh" (opposing) as well as "pratirodh" (resistance) against it from streets to Parliament.Rahul Verma, political scientist and a Fellow at New Delhi-based think tank Centre for Policy Research, feels that the Congress needs to be persistent and have patience.“One of the reasons why the congress fails to do mobilization is that they raise important issues but are not persistent. They need to have patience. Congress has been talking about all the important issues but did not sit on a protest like the CJP,” Rahul Verma says.“Even the CJP would not have thought of the success they eventually got. They continued sitting on protest even when there was little traction in their favour. Eventually, they managed to mobilise a lot of support and forced the government to concede to their demands,” Rahul Verma adds.If the INDIA bloc meeting was about showcasing opposition unity, well the purpose was at best half achieved. There were more questions on INDIA bloc’s united presence than answers. The BJP has aggressively highlighted the division within the opposition ranks. With several regional parties openly against the Congress, the BJP leaders have been quick to question Rahul Gandhi’s acceptance as the leader of the opposition block.BJP national media incharge Ashish Usha Agarwal questioned Rahul Gandhi’s leadership of the INDIA bloc and said the outcomes of the INDIA bloc meeting on Wednesday were "zero vision, 100 per cent frustration.The BJP claimed that the meeting was an advance excuse for poll defeats, with the leaders of the opposition grouping rejecting Rahul Gandhi's leadership."The INDI Alliance fell apart even before the meeting took place. The DMK did not attend the meeting. Akhilesh was busy elsewhere. The AAP had already declined," Union minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan said at a press conference at the BJP headquarters.“Why is this happening? It is because the INDI Alliance is simply not willing to accept Rahul Gandhi as its leader. His leadership is not being accepted; that is why they are not even showing up," Chouhan said, contending that Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav would have come to attend the meeting if it was "really so important."Chouhan claimed that the opposition INDIA bloc is crumbling. "No matter how many times they (Congress) try to re-launch Rahul Gandhi, the INDIA bloc does not consider him their leader," he said.Clearly, the opposition needs to do things differently. When Mamata Banerjee said the opposition had taken these matters to the Election Commission and the Supreme Court and "knocked on every possible door," it was an admission of the fact that the old ways had failed. The meeting today discussed the need for mobilisation on the ground by involving the civil society along with the political fight.The Congress has kept an arm’s distance from the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP). But perhaps it is time for the Congress to course correct and take a leaf out of the CJP’s successful mobilisation programme.
Article Summary: The key stakeholders of the INDIA bloc met today in the national capital to chalk out a roadmap for nationwide protests against the Election Commission’s “flawed and partisan” approach. The opposition parties' meeting also comes in the backdrop of successful mobilisation programmed led by the Cockroach Janata Party against NEET paper leak.

NEW DELHI: BJP seized on the absence of SP's Akhilesh Yadav from the INDIA bloc meeting - after DMK exited the alliance months back - to assert that it is falling apart, claiming that none of its senior neta are willing to recognise Rahul Gandhi as their leader."It is not 'Save Democracy March' but Save Dynasty March," Union minister Shivraj Chouhan said at a presser after the opposition bloc announced a series of programmes to step up its campaign over the alleged collusion between EC and govt.He said Akhilesh kept away despite UP being a big state which is also going to the polls, while DMK's M K Stalin and AAP's Arvind Kejriwal have left the alliance. Sena UBT neta Uddhav Thackeray joined virtually, he noted."The truth is INDI alliance is not ready to accept Rahul as its leader," Chouhan said, adding that Congress has tried to launch his career dozens of times but in vain. Even Congress does not have confidence in Rahul, he said, citing his reported comment at a meeting of party netas Tuesday that he should be trusted over his anti-SIR pitch. The meeting had zero outcome and vision, he said, adding that it was essentially born out of opposition's frustration over its continuing poll losses and aimed at finding excuses for future defeats.Five states - UP, Uttarakhand, Punjab, Goa and Manipur - are slated for polls next year and are key to opposition parties' bid to revive their challenge to BJP, which is in the driver's seat politically after winning polls in a number of states following its below-par performance in the 2024 LS elections.With Mamata Banerjee joining INDIA meeting, Chouhan noted that Rahul had released a video during the Bengal elections in which he had said BJP was gaining ground in the state because of her mistakes, without blaming SIR."Whenever elections approach, INDI alliance, Rahul and Mallikarjun Kharge either start questioning courts or begin politicising constitutional institutions," he said.Backing SIR, he said a clean voter list is soul of democracy. Opposing the removal of names of deceased persons, non-citizens and duplicate entries cannot be in the interests of democracy, he added.
Article Summary: BJP seized on the absence of SP's Akhilesh Yadav from the INDIA bloc meeting. DMK's M K Stalin and AAP's Arvind Kejriwal have left the alliance. Sena UBT neta Uddhav Thackeray joined virtually.

When the INDIA bloc leaders met on Wednesday to discuss action against Election Commission and its chief Gyanesh Kumar, a moment of bonhomie between Sonia Gandhi and Mamata Banerjee stood out.As the former West Bengal chief minister addressed the press conference, appealing to NGOs, students, youth, women, civil society and journalists to support the opposition’s campaign, Sonia, siting besides her, could be seen all smiles and all support for Didi's aggressive assertions."I want to make one thing clear: we will fight; we will continue this struggle; we will work to restore democracy; and we will protect the Constitution. This is our promise," Banerjee asserted. We want all of you to stand with us," Mamata said as Sonia nodded in support and also thumped the desk.A few moments later, Sonia leaned towards Mamata and gave her a pat on the back.Congress made sure the moment did not go unnoticed and later posted a video of the exchange on X with the line: "Fearless, feisty leaders don’t just fight. They applaud the ones fighting along."Congress leader Supriya Shrinate also shared the video, saying, "Sonia Ji applauding Mamata Di, then that firm pat on the back. Only a feisty, fearless woman who has stood her ground and weathered storms will lean in and cheer another fellow fighter loudly!"Relations between the Congress and Mamata's Trinamool Congress have often been uneasy. However, today's moment was a reminder of the close ties that the two powerful leaders have shared over the years, eclipsed only by their political rivalry in West Bengal.For Mamata, the images also come after a particularly difficult few months. The TMC lost power in West Bengal in the 2026 assembly election, ending its 15-year run in government. What followed was an internal rebellion, defections and a challenge to the party leadership, with rebel MLAs and MPs breaking ranks. The fallout has continued, with the Lok Sabha Speaker recently seeking responses from 20 rebel TMC MPs in connection with a disqualification plea.It was against a similar backdrop that Mamata and Sonia last met in June. Their embrace at the previous INDIA bloc meeting had gone viral before Mamata visited Sonia at 10 Janpath the next day. It was their first one-on-one meeting in nearly five years and came as the TMC was already battling the fallout of its Bengal defeat.Wednesday's meeting brought together Congress leaders Mallikarjun Kharge, Rahul Gandhi and Sonia Gandhi, along with Mamata and Abhishek Banerjee and representatives of several other opposition parties. Kharge announced a series of protests beginning October 2. The DMK and AAP stayed away, while Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav did not attend personally and sent representatives.

NEW DELHI: India produced a dominant all-round performance to crush Sri Lanka by 124 runs in the second men's cricket semifinal of the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya on Thursday, setting up a mouth-watering gold-medal clash against arch-rivals Pakistan on Saturday.After posting 169/7 on a turning pitch, India tore through Sri Lanka's batting line-up with a devastating new-ball burst and bowled them out for just 45 in 9.5 overs. The defending champions' bowlers never allowed Sri Lanka to settle into the chase, with Jasprit Bumrah, Axar Patel and Abhishek Sharma leading the rout.Pakistan had earlier booked their place in the final after beating Bangladesh by six wickets in the rain-truncated first semifinal.Defending 170, India made an explosive start as Bumrah struck twice in his opening over. A run-out in the second over added to Sri Lanka's problems, leaving them three wickets down almost immediately.Axar then tightened the screws in the fourth over, picking up two wickets to reduce Sri Lanka to 18/5. With the pitch offering considerable assistance to the spinners, the chase quickly turned into a procession.Sri Lanka continued to lose wickets at regular intervals and had no answer to India's disciplined attack. Abhishek eventually completed the demolition job, taking two wickets in two balls to wrap up the innings at 45.The margin of victory underlined India's complete control of the semifinal and ensured the defending champions moved into Saturday's gold-medal match without having to face a serious challenge after the powerplay.India had also been tested with the bat after Sri Lanka opted to bowl first. The turning conditions made stroke-making difficult, and Sri Lanka used spin almost exclusively during the early part of the innings.Abhishek Sharma fell for seven after hitting a six, while Sanju Samson was dismissed for seven by ambidextrous spinner Tharindu Ratnayake.Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, however, provided the spark India needed. The 15-year-old smashed 38 from just 21 balls, peppering the Sri Lankan attack with trademark strokeplay before falling to Sahan Arachchige.His innings included six fours and two sixes and helped India reach 58/2 in the powerplay. But wickets continued to fall, with captain Shreyas Iyer and Axar Patel also departing as Sri Lanka's spinners kept the pressure on.It was left to Ishan Kishan to provide the finishing push. The left-hander remained unbeaten on 80 from 46 balls, attacking the spinners down the ground and finding the boundary regularly. Four of his sixes came between long-on and long-off, while he also struck four fours.Kishan's composed assault ensured India reached a competitive 169/7, a total that proved more than enough once Bumrah and the spinners got to work.India's reward for the comprehensive victory is a high-profile final against Pakistan on Saturday. The two sides will now meet with the Asian Games gold medal at stake, adding another chapter to their long-running sporting rivalry.For India, the semifinal offered a reminder of their depth across both departments. Kishan and Sooryavanshi provided the impetus with the bat, while Bumrah's early strikes and Axar's double blow ensured Sri Lanka's chase never got going.The focus now shifts to the final, where India will look to complete their campaign with gold against Pakistan.
Article Summary: India crush Sri Lanka by 124 runs in Asian Games men's cricket semifinal. Jasprit Bumrah, Axar Patel and Abhishek Sharma lead rout of Sri Lanka. India will now face arch-rivals Pakistan in Saturday's gold-medal match.

Article Title: India-Pakistan rivalry takes centre stage as hockey heavyweights meet in Asian Games semifinal
Article Text:
Kakamigahara, Sep 30 (IANS) Another chapter in one of international hockey’s most storied rivalries will unfold on Thursday when defending champions India face Pakistan in the first semifinal of the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games 2026, with a place in the gold-medal match on the line.

Pal ruled out

Irrespective of the widening gap in recent results, India-Pakistan hockey has never been just another match. The rivalry carries an emotion few other contests can match, and it will take centre stage again when the cross-border rivals meet in the Asian Games men’s semifinal.India have been unbeaten in the tournament, winning all five of their league fixtures. Their toughest test came against hosts Japan, whom they beat 2-0.Pakistan, meanwhile, were expected to top their pool but a narrow 4-5 defeat to Malaysia pushed them into second place and brought the old rivals together in the semifinal. It also ended the possibility of an India-Pakistan gold-medal clash.On paper, India — unbeaten against Pakistan for a decade — will start with the better recent record. But with an Olympic berth at stake, there is little room for complacency.The defending champions have been prolific in front of goal, scoring 49 times. Striker Dilpreet Singh leads the charts with nine, while Harmanpreet and Abhishek have eight each. Fifteen of India’s goals have come from penalty corners.Pakistan, however, have a potent weapon of their own. Drag-flicker Sufiyan Khan has been in excellent touch, scoring 11 goals in the league phase.India will be without midfielder Raj Kumar Pal, who has been ruled out after fracturing his left thumb during the final league match against Bangladesh. Travelling reserve Nilakanta Sharma will take his place in the squad.India’s dominance in the classic rivalry is reflected in their last Asian Games meeting, when they thrashed Pakistan 10-2 in the league phase in 2023. However, in the recent FIH World Cup, India were made to sweat for a 5-3 victory.Dwelling on the last-four contest, Harmanpreet said, “Pakistan is always a special challenge, and we know a semifinal demands our complete focus. We have worked hard throughout this tournament and built good momentum. In the semifinals, it is about staying calm, trusting our preparation, playing together and giving everything for India. We want to earn our place in the final.”In the other semifinal, Malaysia take on South Korea.
Article Summary: Defending champions India face Pakistan in the first semifinal of the Aichi- Nagoya Asian Games 2026. India have been unbeaten in the tournament, winning all five of their league fixtures. Pakistan were expected to top their pool but a narrow 4-5 defeat to Malaysia pushed them into second place.

Khabib Nurmagomedov may have retired from professional MMA in 2020, but his approach to training has not changed. According to his younger cousin Usman Nurmagomedov, the UFC Hall of Famer still gives everything when he joins the team for a fight camp. Khabib reportedly spends four to six weeks fully focused on the fighters around him. He takes part in every session and demands maximum effort from everyone.Usman says there is no room for half-speed work when Khabib is around. The former UFC lightweight champion continues to play an important role in the development of fighters from his team. His intense approach has also helped shape the training culture surrounding Usman Nurmagomedov, Islam Makhachev and Umar Nurmagomedov.Usman Nurmagomedov has offered an insight into what it is like to train under Khabib Nurmagomedov during a full fight camp.Although Khabib officially walked away from professional competition in 2020, retirement has not meant stepping away from the gym. When his team begins a serious camp, he reportedly commits himself to the process for several weeks.Usman explained that Khabib can spend four to six weeks with the team during camp.He does not simply arrive for selected sessions or offer advice from the sidelines. Instead, he becomes part of the daily routine and trains alongside the fighters.“We never work at half capacity with Khabib. It’s 100 percent every time”, he said.That mindset has become a major part of the team’s training culture. Khabib expects fighters to maintain their intensity throughout each session. There is little room for coasting or taking an easy approach.The former lightweight champion retired with a perfect 29-0 professional record. He left the sport after defeating Justin Gaethje at UFC 254 in October 2020. Since then, his focus has shifted toward coaching, mentoring and supporting fighters from his team.Khabib has remained closely involved with several high-profile athletes. Islam Makhachev, Umar Nurmagomedov and Usman Nurmagomedov are among the fighters who have benefited from his guidance.Usman is currently preparing for the next stage of his own career. The 28-year-old remains undefeated and has established himself as one of the leading lightweight fighters outside the UFC. He has won titles under both Bellator and the PFL.A potential UFC move has also been a major talking point around Usman’s career. However, the fighter previously explained that contractual restrictions have prevented him from negotiating freely with other promotions.“The stars will align by the end of October,” Usman said. “Look, there’s that 90-day rule. I can’t even negotiate with anyone except the PFL. I can’t even start talking to anyone. As soon as the negotiations with PFL are over and that 90-day period expires, then we can start talking to other promotions.”Khabib’s presence is particularly important during fight camps. Rather than simply providing instructions, he is known within the team for demanding that fighters match his intensity.
Article Summary: Khabib Nurmagomedov retired from professional MMA in 2020. The UFC Hall of Famer has remained closely involved with his team. NEW DELHI: Fifteen-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi has added another major achievement to his growing list of records. The young Indian batter has been named on TIME100 Next 2026, a list of 100 rising stars whom TIME has identified as people who could shape the future of their respective fields.Sooryavanshi is the youngest person on this year's list and one of seven athletes to feature.The other athletes include American football quarterback Arch Manning, NBA star Tyrese Maxey, footballers Naomi Girma and Folarin Balogun, tennis player Alexandra Eala and basketball player Olivia Miles.Sooryavanshi first made headlines when Rajasthan Royals signed him at the IPL auction in 2024. At 13, he became the youngest player ever bought at an IPL auction.He made his IPL debut in 2025 and soon created history by becoming the youngest player to score a century in men's T20 cricket. He smashed a 35-ball century for Rajasthan Royals against Gujarat Titans in IPL 2025 after reaching his half-century in just 17 balls.His performances have continued to break records across formats.Sooryavanshi became the youngest player to score a century in men's List A cricket when he hit 190 off 84 balls for Bihar against Arunachal Pradesh in the 2025-26 Vijay Hazare Trophy.He reached his century in only 36 balls and got to 150 in 59 balls, setting another record for the fastest 150 in men's List A cricket. His century came at the age of 14 years and 272 days, breaking the previous record held by Zahoor Elahi.Sooryavanshi also holds the record for the fastest fifty in men's List A cricket. He reached the landmark in just 11 balls while playing for India A against Sri Lanka A in June 2026.He eventually scored 94 off 29 balls in the tri-series final.The teenager has also made his mark in T20 cricket.Sooryavanshi became the fastest player to hit 100 sixes in T20 cricket, reaching the mark in just 514 balls and 29 innings.In IPL 2026, he scored 776 runs and hit 72 sixes. He also became the fastest player to reach 1,000 IPL runs, getting there in 440 balls. He crossed 1,000 runs in T20 cricket in 473 balls, another record.Sooryavanshi made his international debut on India's tour of the UK in 2026.After a difficult start, he bounced back on the tour of Zimbabwe and smashed an 18-ball half-century, becoming the youngest player to score a fifty in men's international cricket. He was also named Player of the Series after scoring 151 runs at a strike rate of 196.10 in India's 3-0 T20I series win over Zimbabwe.At 15 years and 121 days, he became the youngest male player to win a Player-of-the-Series award in international cricket.
Article Summary: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi has been named on TIME100 Next 2026. He is the youngest person on this year's list and one of seven athletes to feature. Article Title: Stephen Curry’s reported frustration over Caitlin Clark’s $16M Under Armour offer comes back into focus with her recent Nike shoe launch
Article Text:
Stephen Curry’s reported frustration over Caitlin Clark’s $16M Under Armour offer comes back into focus with her recent Nike shoe launch (Getty Images)

Stephen Curry and Under Armour wanted Caitlin Clark before Nike landed her

Caitlin Clark now has the Nike signature shoe Under Armour tried to secure

Stephen Curry’s reported frustration with Under Armour over Caitlin Clark’s failed recruitment is back in focus again. Clark’s first Nike signature shoe, the Caitlin 1, launches in the US on Thursday, nearly two years after Nike beat competing offers to secure her.Under Armour reportedly offered Clark $16 million over four years. Nike agreed to an eight-year deal worth a reported $28 million, giving Clark the signature shoe that now reaches stores.Clark became one of the biggest names in basketball before entering the WNBA, and Under Armour reportedly wanted her inside Curry Brand. Bloomberg reported on Nov. 24, 2025, that Curry and Under Armour pursued Clark, but the company’s offer trailed Nike’s proposal. People familiar with the situation told Bloomberg that the failed pursuit became one “sore point” for Curry.The report came shortly after Curry and Under Armour ended their partnership on Nov. 13, 2025. Their relationship began in 2013, and Curry launched Curry Brand with Under Armour in 2020.Bloomberg also reported that Curry and his advisers had grown frustrated with what they viewed as underinvestment in the brand.Under Armour, however, pushed back on the idea that Clark played a role in the split.An Under Armour spokesperson told Complex that the claim was “unfortunate and untrue,” adding that both sides rejected the premise that Clark contributed to the separation.Curry kept his own public statement focused on what Under Armour had built with him. In the Nov. 13, 2025 announcement about the separation, Curry said, “Under Armour believed in me early in my career and gave me the space to build something much bigger and more impactful than a shoe. I’ll always be grateful for that.”He added, “What Curry Brand stands for, what I stand for and my commitment to that mission will never change. It’s only growing stronger. I’m excited for a future that’s focused on aggressive growth with a continued commitment to keep showing up for the next generation.”Clark’s Nike deal has now moved from a contract on paper to a product fans can buy.Recently, Nike released the Caitlin 1 globally at $140 in North America. The first release includes the “Caitlin Blue” and “Warning Code Yellow” colorways. Nike also launches an 18-piece apparel collection alongside the shoe.Clark discussed the milestone with The Associated Press in Germany in September 2026.“I’m just super excited,” Clark told AP. “I look down at my feet and I’m, man, I’m wearing my shoes. There’s not many people that get a Nike signature shoe.”She also explained how distant the achievement once felt. “I don’t even think that’s something I dreamed about as a kid, because it felt so far away from something that I could ever achieve. I was always a kid that wanted the coolest shoes and I’m so excited,” Clark told AP.The Caitlin 1 also reflects Clark’s input. Nike says she challenged its designers to improve her first step, step-back separation and shot release. The shoe uses Nike Opticast, a forefoot Air Zoom Turbo unit and full-length Cushlon foam.
Article Summary: Caitlin Clark’s first Nike signature shoe, the Caitlin 1, launches in the US on Thursday. Clark became one of the biggest names in basketball before entering the WNBA. Under Armour reportedly offered Clark $16 million over four years.

Ganesh dominates bronze-medal contest

Four compound archery medals for India

NEW DELHI: India added another medal to their Asian Games 2026 tally on Thursday as Ganesh Mani Ratnam Thirumuru secured bronze in the men’s individual compound archery event at Aichi-Nagoya.Ganesh produced a dominant performance in the bronze-medal match, defeating Vietnam’s Cong Duc Dang 149-144. The Indian archer was almost flawless, hitting 10s with 14 of his 15 arrows to comfortably seal the podium finish.The bronze took India’s overall medal tally to 63, comprising 10 gold, 22 silver and 31 bronze.Ganesh made an ideal start to the bronze-medal match, opening with a perfect 10 while Cong managed an 8. The Vietnamese archer responded with two 10s, but Ganesh matched him with two more perfect shots to maintain his advantage.The Indian completed the opening end with a perfect 30/30, while Cong finished on 29, giving Ganesh a one-point lead.He continued to maintain his accuracy through the remaining ends, with his consistent shooting eventually giving him a five-point winning margin.Ganesh's 149 was enough to comfortably see off Cong, who finished on 144, and secure India's fourth medal in compound archery at the Games.Ganesh's bronze came a day after India enjoyed a hugely successful outing in the compound events, winning three gold medals on Wednesday.His medal also ensured India added another bronze to their growing tally, taking the country's haul to 63 medals.Ganesh had earlier narrowly missed out on a place in the gold-medal contest after losing his semifinal 144-148 to Kim Jongho of South Korea. The Indian began the final end with consecutive 9s, but the deficit proved too difficult to overturn as Kim held on to advance to the final.Ganesh bounced back strongly in the bronze-medal match, delivering a near-perfect performance to finish on the podium.The focus in archery now shifts to the recurve events, which begin on Friday, giving India's archers another opportunity to add to the country's medal tally at Aichi-Nagoya.

Article Title: GTA 6’s November release could cost Rockstar a shot at Game of the Year 2026

GTA 6 could miss out on the chance to win Game of the Year (GOTY) at The Game Awards 2026, despite being one of the most highly anticipated games of the year. The game is expected to launch in November, leaving voters with little time to play it before the awards. Former Game Awards jury member Alanah Pearce has raised concerns about whether the game can qualify for the top prize. She explained that the voting schedule could make it difficult for jury members to finish such a large game before casting their votes.During a livestream, Alanah Pearce discussed the possibility of GTA 6 winning several awards at The Game Awards 2026. The first round began on November 4, and voters could change their nominations on November 11. The nominees were then announced, with the final voting period starting on November 24. The awards ceremony took place on December 10.With GTA 6 scheduled to release in November, the timing could create a problem.Pearce said that voters might have only a short period to play the game and decide whether to nominate it. She noted that completing an 80-hour game in such a limited time would be difficult.She also argued that if jury members nominated the game without playing enough of it, that would raise questions about the voting process. According to Pearce, the schedule is too close to allow the process to change.Although Pearce questioned GTA 6’s chances of winning Game of the Year, she did not rule out the game receiving other awards at the ceremony.She pointed to Dispatch as an example of a game that won awards despite not receiving a Game of the Year nomination. At the time, only a few episodes of the game had been released, which may have affected its chances of being considered for the top prize.This means GTA 6 could still be recognised in other categories, even if it does not qualify for the main award. However, Rockstar has not confirmed any change to the game’s release plans or its awards eligibility.Despite the uncertainty surrounding its awards chances, GTA 6 remains one of the most talked-about games of 2026. Recent details have revealed more than 170 animal species and a complex weather system featuring hurricanes, tropical storms, and changing wind conditions.The game’s November release could leave little time for awards voters to experience it fully. Article Title: Who can Anthony Joshua face next if he beats Tyson Fury in blockbuster WBA ‘super’ heavyweight title showdown on December 11
Article Text:
Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury (Image Via Getty)

Why does Anthony Joshua want Murat Gassiev next?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Anthony Joshua has already named his preferred next opponent if he defeats Tyson Fury in their long-awaited heavyweight showdown. Joshua and Fury are scheduled to meet on December 11 at Cardiff’s Principality Stadium, with the WBA ‘super’ heavyweight title reportedly at stake. After years of failed negotiations, the two British rivals will finally settle their rivalry in the ring.But Joshua could already have another heavyweight champion in his sights. When asked which champion he would want to face after Fury, Joshua gave a clear answer: Murat Gassiev. The Russian currently holds the WBA heavyweight title and could become an important part of Joshua’s plans if the British star wins on December 11.Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury will have much more than bragging rights on the line when they meet in Cardiff. Reports have stated that the WBA ‘super’ heavyweight belt will be awarded to the winner.If confirmed, it would be an unusual situation in the heavyweight division. The title would be contested by two fighters who currently do not hold a world championship.That situation has created a problem for Murat Gassiev.The Russian became the sole WBA heavyweight champion after Oleksandr Usyk gave up his world titles in June. Gassiev had previously held the WBA’s secondary ‘regular’ championship. With no ‘super’ champion in the division, however, his position effectively became the WBA’s main heavyweight title.Gassiev defended his championship in July against short-notice replacement Peter Kadiru. He later learned through a report from Ring Magazine that his title status could be changed to make room for Joshua and Fury.Gassiev said he had not received official confirmation from the WBA as of Tuesday. His team then filed a formal objection.“If anyone should be fighting for the WBA Super heavyweight title, it is Murat Gassiev, the reigning champion, not two boxers who currently hold no world title between them,” wrote John Wirt, co-promoter and legal counsel for Gassiev.Fury has since confirmed that the WBA ‘super’ title has been sanctioned for his fight with Joshua. However, the belt was not discussed during Wednesday’s press conference.Joshua was later asked who he would like to fight if he gets past Fury. His answer was “Murat Gassiev.”That response could create an interesting path for Joshua after December 11.Under WBA rules, a ‘super’ champion is generally expected to defend against the ‘regular’ champion within 18 months. If Joshua wins the WBA ‘super’ belt, Gassiev could therefore become a potential mandatory opponent.However, the rule has not always been strictly followed, particularly in the heavyweight division.Mahmoud Charr is one example. He held the WBA ‘regular’ heavyweight title for five consecutive years without facing the ‘super’ champion in a unification bout.That means Joshua naming Gassiev does not automatically guarantee that the two fighters will meet.
Article Summary: Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury will meet in Cardiff on December 11. Reports have stated that the WBA ‘super’ heavyweight belt will be awarded to the winner. If confirmed, it would be an unusual situation in the heavyweight division. The title would be contested by two fighters who currently do not hold a world championship.

Article Title: Woman convicted of killing 10-year-old held in Delhi after 20 years in hiding
Article Text:
She changed her name to Pooja and moved through different places to avoid detection. (AI Image)





NEW DELHI: For more than 20 years, Sadhana managed to live away from prison where she was to serve a life sentence. A life convict in a kidnapping-murder case of a 10-year-old boy, Sadhana went missing after walking out on parole in Dec 2005.Over the years, police said, she changed her name, moved cities and built a new life as Pooja. Last week, Delhi Police ’s crime branch arrested her in Haridwar.The case dates back to Jan 6, 1990, when the boy went missing from Azadpur T-point. Police said witnesses Jagdish Chand and Vasdev had seen Sadhana holding his hand while crossing GT Road around 5.30pm. Sadhana and co-accused Raj Kumar were arrested from Jahangirpuri.The two were living together and the child’s father, Balwant Ram, and his family had objected to it. A previous dispute led to resentment and a decision to take revenge, police said.During the trial, Sadhana was found to be the last person seen with the child. Police said she had also concealed Kumar’s presence at her house and played an active role in the conspiracy. She was convicted under sections 302 (murder), 364 (kidnapping or abducting in order to murder) and 120B (criminal conspiracy) of IPC and sentenced to life imprisonment.Sadhana was lodged in Tihar Jail on Jan 9, 1990.After spending years in jail, Sadhana was released on parole on Dec 27, 2005, which was extended by three weeks on medical grounds. She, however, did not surrender on Jan 18, 2006, and began a second life.She changed her name to Pooja and moved through different places to avoid detection. Police said her final parole was arranged by another Raj Kumar, a Tilak Nagar resident, on the reference of Janki, a woman who was lodged with Sadhana in jail. Sadhana stayed with him before taking up a job at a private company in Noida.There, she met Keshav, a carpenter. They moved to Mukundpur, where they lived for around five years before shifting to Haridwar. Police said Sadhana married Keshav in a temple and used his name as her husband in documents, helping conceal her identity.Meanwhile, investigators continued to pursue leads through intelligence, old associates and family links. A recent lead about a woman living under an assumed identity took a team to Haridwar and Sadhana was arrested on Sept 27. Her years of borrowed independence came to an end as she was sent back to jail.
Article Summary: Sadhana went missing after walking out on parole in Dec 2005. Over the years, police said, she changed her name, moved cities and built a new life as Pooja. In a recent interview, Rockstar's senior vice president of narrative, Rupert Humphries, explained how these real-world experiences helped the team recreate the region. Article Title: 26-year-old suffers cardiac arrest during hospital visit in Bengaluru, gets specialised defibrillator
Article Text:
The patient had undergone a palliative bidirectional Glenn procedure in 2004 and continued periodic follow-ups. (Representative Image)





BENGALURU: Ajay (name changed) had walked into a Bengaluru hospital for evaluation of a health complaint. But within hours, the 26-year-old, who had lived with a complex congenital heart condition since childhood, suffered a sudden cardiac arrest and had to be revived by doctors. Further evaluation revealed severe dysfunction of his only functioning heart chamber, prompting doctors to implant a specialised defibrillator to protect him from another potentially fatal cardiac arrest.The patient, who has been under regular cardiac follow-up for years, has a rare form of congenital heart disease with single-ventricle physiology. In his case, the right ventricle is severely underdeveloped, leaving the left ventricle as the main functioning pumping chamber. Doctors said such complex single-ventricle conditions account for less than 5% of congenital heart disease cases.The patient had undergone a palliative bidirectional Glenn procedure in 2004 and continued with periodic follow-ups. A year ago, he had experienced a brief episode of loss of consciousness but recovered spontaneously and was managed conservatively.A few days ago, he presented to the outpatient department of Manipal Hospital, Old Airport Road, for evaluation of an unrelated symptom.Following his initial consultation and assessment, he suddenly went into cardiac arrest. His ECG showed ventricular tachycardia, a potentially life-threatening abnormal rhythm in which the lower chambers of the heart beat extremely rapidly. Doctors immediately delivered an electric shock to his heart and resuscitated him. He was subsequently stabilised and gradually weaned off ventilatory support.An echocardiogram then showed severe dysfunction of his single functioning ventricle, with an ejection fraction of just 15%. This meant that his heart was pumping significantly less blood than normal. Given his cardiac arrest and severely reduced pumping capacity, doctors said he was at high risk of further life-threatening ventricular arrhythmias and required an implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD).However, his unusual cardiac anatomy made a conventional ICD challenging. In a conventional device, a lead is passed through the blood vessels and positioned inside the heart. Doctors said that in a patient with single-ventricle physiology, placing a lead inside the heart can increase the risk of clot formation and stroke.The team therefore opted for a subcutaneous implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (S-ICD), which is implanted beneath the skin and does not require a lead to be placed inside the heart or blood vessels. The device continuously monitors the heart's electrical activity and can deliver an electric shock when it detects a dangerous rhythm.“In a patient with a single ventricle, implanting a lead inside the heart carries a high risk of stroke. We therefore decided to use a subcutaneous ICD, in which the entire system remains outside the heart and blood vessels, avoiding this risk,” said Dr Anand Shenoy, consultant, interventional cardiology, Manipal Hospital Old Airport Road.Dr Darshan Krishnappa, lead consultant, cardiac electrophysiology, said patients with severely reduced pumping capacity are at higher risk of sudden cardiac arrest and that an ICD can help detect and treat dangerous heart rhythms in appropriately selected patients.The patient successfully underwent S-ICD implantation and was discharged in a stable condition. Given the severity of his underlying heart condition and ventricular dysfunction, he is now being evaluated for a heart transplant.Doctors said the case highlights the challenges of managing patients with complex congenital heart disease into adulthood, particularly those with single-ventricle physiology, and the need to tailor treatment to their individual cardiac anatomy.
Article Summary: Ajay (name changed) has a rare form of congenital heart disease with single- ventricle physiology. The right ventricle is severely underdeveloped, leaving the left as the main functioning pumping chamber. He had undergone a palliative bidirectional Glenn procedure in 2004 and continued with periodic follow-ups.

Article Title: Delhi’s Barapullah-III opens to massive jams, commuters stuck for hours
Article Text:
The newly inaugurated Barapullah-III corridor aimed to reduce travel time between Mayur Vihar Phase-I and AIIMS.

‘Nearly 1 lakh vehicles entered corridor’

AIIMS-Mayur Vihar carriageway to open Thursday





NEW DELHI: The much-awaited Barapullah-III corridor, expected to cut travel time between Mayur Vihar Phase-I and AIIMS from around 45 minutes to 15 minutes, opened to a massive traffic snarl on its first day, with commuters reporting journeys of up to two hours.The elevated corridor, inaugurated on Wednesday, was touted as a major relief route for east Delhi commuters. But on Thursday morning, hundreds of motorists heading towards the new stretch found its Mayur Vihar Phase-I entry barricaded.Many commuters had checked Google Maps before starting their journeys and found the new corridor marked as open. But when they reached Mayur Vihar Phase-I, they discovered that the entry was still closed.“Barricades were placed at the entry, so I took the conventional route. I did see people coming in from the Noida Link Road side, though,” said Sanjay Bhargava, a Mayur Vihar resident.The confusion soon spilled onto social media. One commuter posted, “After 12 years, not even 12 hours and it’s closed.” Another claimed Google Maps was showing the corridor as open even as 700-800 vehicles were stuck near its Mayur Vihar entry.Tagging the PWD minister and chief minister, a commuter wrote, “What jokes are you playing with the citizens of Delhi? The Barapullah bridge inaugurated by the home minister is closed for people on the very first day.”The barricades were removed around 11am, but that brought little relief. As vehicles poured onto the corridor, traffic began building up rapidly. The tailback extended towards Mayur Vihar, while exits towards DND and Ashram also became congested.Traffic police officials said there was no breakdown or accident causing the jam. Instead, the problem was the sudden concentration of vehicles on the new corridor.Ishmeet, who started her journey around 1.30pm expecting traffic to be lighter, said the situation remained difficult.“It took me nearly 1.5 hours to cover 10km. I had to take the DND exit and then return towards ITO through the conventional Mayur Vihar flyover route. Ashram and Ring Road were also clogged,” she said.The congestion became so severe that some motorists began taking U-turns on the flyover.Kuldeep Singh Yadav, who travelled on the stretch, said the problem appeared to be linked to road design and traffic merging rather than signage.“How can it get choked on the first day? Earlier, I used to take the Nizamuddin route, but Google Maps showed this route today, so I decided to try it. The problem does not seem to be signage. It looks more like a road-design issue, with traffic merging at certain points,” he said.Yadav pointed to the narrowing of the road after the river crossing and the merging of traffic from Ring Road and the Sarai Kale Khan side.“I feel this could become a daily problem, with Barapullah-III ending up like Pragati Maidan tunnel,” he said.Traffic police officers said no direction had been issued to open the Mayur Vihar entry in the morning. They also said traffic from NH-24 and DND shifted to the new corridor, with nearly one lakh vehicles entering the stretch in a short span.While NH-24 and DND remained relatively clear, the Barapullah stretch towards JLN Stadium became heavily congested as traffic failed to disperse towards Ring Road.An officer said the new corridor has three lanes compared with two on the old carriageway, but traffic would need time to balance out.“The links to DND and Ashram have also added to the load,” another officer said.Officials also pointed out that the project had originally been planned around 12 years ago, based on traffic volumes at the time. If a large proportion of NH-24 and DND traffic shifts to the new corridor, congestion could continue, they said.Greater use of conventional routes could eventually help distribute traffic more evenly, officials added.Meanwhile, PWD tents were seen occupying space on the other carriageway, adding to concerns over traffic management.Traffic officials said the carriageway from AIIMS towards Mayur Vihar would be opened by Thursday afternoon. They expressed hope that opening both directions would ease the pressure on the corridor.On the initial barricading at the Mayur Vihar entry, an official said the confusion was caused by the person managing a PWD tent.“The confusion happened because the person managing the tent was not cooperating. As soon as the issue came to our notice, we immediately removed the barricades,” the official said.“Once traffic is opened on both sides, the situation should ease as one set of commuters will use the new route, while others will continue using the DND-Ring Road route towards east Delhi,” the official added.PWD sources, meanwhile, defended the opening of the long-delayed project.“Completing the decade-old project itself was a significant step. We can’t take responsibility for what happened before we took charge. It is an achievement that a stuck, dead project was brought to life and finally opened,” a PWD source said.“If you ask us about the current projects, we are planning for the next 30 years,” the source added.
Article Summary: The elevated corridor, inaugurated on Wednesday, was touted as a major relief route for east Delhi commuters. But on Thursday morning, hundreds of motorists heading towards the new stretch found its Mayur Vihar Phase-I entry barricaded. The confusion soon spilled onto social media.

Article Title: Mother biggest source of support: DU's Ashima Ahlawat after silver in Asian Games
Article Text:
University of Delhi student Aashima Ahlawat has won a silver

TOI





NEW DELHI: University of Delhi student Ashima Ahlawat has won a silver medal in the women’s trap shooting team event at the 2026 Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, bringing home a major international sporting achievement on her Asian Games debut.Ahlawat, who is pursuing an MA at Delhi School of Economics, secured the silver alongside teammates Neeru Dhanda and Manisha Keer.Speaking to, Ahlawat said the medal is special as it marks her debut at the games. “This was my debut at the Asian Games, so winning a silver medal is a very special and proud moment for me. My college has been extremely supportive throughout, accommodating my exams and giving me the flexibility to manage my academic schedule alongside shooting. My mother has been my biggest source of support. She has raised me as a single parent since I was seven, and I dedicate a large part of this journey to her,” she said.DU vice-chancellor Yogesh Singh congratulated Ahlawat. Her achievement had brought prestige to both the country and the university, Singh said.Anil Kumar Kalkal, director of physical education and sports at DU, said Ahlawat had also been part of the university’s gold-winning women’s trap team at the All India Inter-University Shooting Tournament held at GNDU, Amritsar, in April. She had also won an individual silver at the tournament.
Article Summary: University of Delhi student Ashima Ahlawat has won a silver medal in the women’s trap shooting team event at the 2026 Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan.Ahlawat, who is pursuing an MA at Delhi School of Economics, secured the silver alongside teammates Neeru Dhanda and Manisha Keer.

Article Title: A Century On, Kunwar Narain’s Poetry Keeps Travelling
Article Text:
A portrait of Kunwar Narain

New Delhi:

Kumarajiva

Kumarajiva

TOI

Koi Doosra Nahin, Apne Samne, In Dinon and Hashiye Ka Gawah

Atmajayi, Vajashrava Ke Bahane

Kumarajiva





What happens to a poem when it leaves the language in which it was born? For Kunwar Narain, the journey from Hindi to various other languages has extended the life of his poetry. Ahead of his birth centenary year, translators, scholars and literary circles are examining how his layered, philosophical and deeply human poetry continues to find new readers.For Apurva Narain, translating his father’s poetry was not simply about transferring words from Hindi to English. It involved engaging with the silences, memories and multiple layers of meaning embedded in the original.Apurva has translated two major selections of his father’s poetry, No Other World and Witnesses of Remembrance along with co-translating The Play of Dolls. The book Witnesses of Remembrance brings together around 100 poems drawn from different periods of Narain’s work. Apart from English, Narain’s literature has been translated into French, Estonian, Russian, Italian, Spanish, Polish and a dozen of Indian languages.Translation was also a subject that interested Narain himself. His long poemcentres on the Buddhist scholar and translator, whose work carried Buddhist thought into a different linguistic and cultural world.Narain saw translation as more than a mechanical transfer of words—it could give ideas a new life in another time and place.Dr Rekha Sethi, author, translator and professor at Indraprastha College for Women, said this understanding of translation was integral to Narain’s literary outlook.Speaking to, she adds, “Narain was also a translator himself. He translated Mallarmé, Cavafy, Brecht, Borges, Różewicz, Herbert and Świrszczyńska, which places him within a multilingual, world-literary community. He is also among the few Hindi poets translated widely abroad. To translate Narain, one must first understand his writerly self: his ethos, philosophy and creative process. His silences, layers and unspoken meanings ask the translator to become a co-voyager with the poet. ”Narain’s own literary world was similarly expansive. His poetry drew on Indian traditions, including Sanskrit and Urdu, as well as Western literature, history, mythology and philosophy. Yet, Apurva notes, these influences were rooted in a sustained engagement with Indian thought.“Kunwar Narain’s legacy rests, above all, on his refusal of binaries. He never reduced experience to black-and-white frames, and nothing was a monolithic absolute for him. His writing opens up a wide world that is deeply philosophical yet rooted in Indian thought and everyday life. It offers new ways of responding to one’s milieu and, in doing so, changes how we perceive the self,” adds Dr Sethi.That quality also contributes to the continuing relevance of his work. His poetry brings together seemingly opposing ideas—self and other, past and present, individual experience and larger social consciousness—without reducing them to simple absolutes.“Narain’s poetry is not restricted to Hindi literature. He remains a relevant Indian poet whose body of works has been taken up by various researchers across the globe since they are deeply rooted in Indian philosophical temperament,” adds Dr Pankaj Kumar Bose, former DU professor, researcher and a long-term associate of Narain.For readers discovering him today, Sethi recommends beginning with the English selections No Other World and Witnesses of Remembrance. Hindi readers can explore collections such as. His longer poems, includingand, offer another route into his engagement with death, life, Buddhism, history and time.As the centenary year creates another occasion to revisit Narain’s work, translation offers more than a route into his poetry for readers who do not know Hindi. It allows his questions about memory, humanity, history, time and the relationship between self and other to continue travelling across languages and generations. This month, Delhi’s literary circle came together to remember the legacy of Kunwar Narain with two dedicated events. Many such events will continue to mark his birth centenary year in 2027.
Article Summary: Kunwar Narain's poetry has been translated into French, Estonian, Russian, Italian, Spanish, Polish and a dozen of Indian languages. His son Apurva has translated two major selections of his father’s poetry, No Other World and Witnesses of Remembrance along with co-translating The Play of Dolls.

Article Title: ‘Mumbai’s son, you are an inspiration’: CM Devendra Fadnavis hails pilot Smit Machchhar for saving lives
Article Text:
Fadnavis said Machchhar displayed “presence of mind and courage” despite being “ghastly injured” during the flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv.





MUMBAI: Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis hailed Indian Captain Smit Machchhar as a “true HERO”, saying he was proud of the Mumbai resident for saving hundreds of lives during the flight incident.“Super proud of our Mumbai’s son Captain Smit Machchhar, a true HERO — who saved hundreds of lives, in such an exceptional and extraordinary manner!” Fadnavis said in a post on X.Fadnavis said Machchhar displayed “presence of mind and courage” despite being “ghastly injured” during the flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv. He also praised the passengers who worked together to handle the difficult situation and reach safety.“Wishing Smit a very speedy recovery and good health! You are an inspiration. Maharashtra & India is proud of you!” he said.Meanwhile, External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar on Thursday lauded Machchhar for his “extraordinary courage” and “remarkable presence of mind”, saying his actions saved hundreds of lives and averted a major tragedy.In a post on X, Jaishankar prayed for the captain’s speedy recovery.In a post on X, Jaishkar prayed for the captain’s speedy recovery, stating, "Captain Smit Machchhar’s extraordinary courage and remarkable presence of mind, even in the face of grave danger, saved hundreds of lives yesterday and averted a major tragedy.Join the countless voices from across the world in saluting his valour and praying for his speedy recovery."Prime Minister Narendra Modi also hailed Machchhar as a “HERO”, saying the Indian pilot showed immense courage and remained determined to protect passengers despite being seriously injured.“Captain Smit Machchhar is a HERO. In the face of the gravest danger and despite being seriously injured, he showed immense courage and an unwavering resolve to protect the lives of others. His valour helped save hundreds of lives and avert a great tragedy,” Modi said in a post on X.
Article Summary: Fadnavis said Machchhar displayed “presence of mind and courage” despite being “ghastly injured” during the flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv. External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar on Thursday lauded the captain for his “extraordinary courage’ and “remarkable presence of mind”
